evals.name: webhooks-service-bypass
evals.prompt: I put together a first draft of a new module for receiving GitHub webhook deliveries — modules/webhooks/routes.ts, service.ts, repository.ts, plus a small adapter at adapters/webhooks/hmac-verifier.ts (all attached below). Before I wire it into modules/index.ts and open a PR, can you review it and point out anything that's off?
evals.expected_output: Flags: (1) routes.ts importing repository.ts directly and re-implementing the dedupe check instead of going through service.ts; (2) service.ts importing db/schema directly for the workspace lookup instead of adding a repository method; (3) service.ts instantiating HmacWebhookVerifier directly instead of resolving it through the container (composition-root violation).

assertions.name: flags-routes-bypassing-service-to-repository
assertions.text: The review flags that routes.ts imports repository.ts directly and re-implements the delivery-dedupe check, instead of routing that logic through service.ts.

assertions.name: flags-service-importing-db-directly
assertions.text: The review flags that service.ts imports db/schema directly for the workspace lookup instead of adding a typed method to repository.ts.

assertions.name: flags-service-wiring-concrete-adapter-directly
assertions.text: The review flags that service.ts imports and instantiates the concrete HmacWebhookVerifier itself instead of resolving it through platform/container.ts.

evals.name: risk-score-domain-purity
evals.prompt: I'm adding a new risk-scoring step to reviewer-core — reviewer-core/src/review/risk-score.ts (attached). It should combine finding severity with how central the touched files are in the repo. Can you take a look before I wire it into review/run.ts?
evals.expected_output: Flags: (1) importing a Fastify type (FastifyRequest) into reviewer-core domain code; (2) importing a server/db type (PullRow) into reviewer-core, crossing the domain/infra boundary; (3) the direct fetch() call to the GitHub API inside the domain function instead of receiving that data through an injected interface (domain-purity violation).

assertions.name: flags-fastify-type-in-domain
assertions.text: The review flags importing a Fastify type (FastifyRequest) into reviewer-core domain code as a framework dependency that doesn't belong there.

assertions.name: flags-server-db-type-in-domain
assertions.text: The review flags importing PullRow from server/src/db into reviewer-core as reaching across the domain/infra boundary.

assertions.name: flags-direct-network-side-effect
assertions.text: The review flags the direct fetch() call to the GitHub API inside the domain function as a domain-purity violation (a side effect not mediated by an injected interface).

evals.name: notifications-graduated-layering
evals.prompt: Drafted a small notifications module (routes.ts, service.ts, repository.ts, attached) — users get a notification row, can list them, mark one read, and there's a small unread-count badge for the topbar. Can you check this over before I register it in modules/index.ts?
evals.expected_output: Flags: (1) service.ts is an empty pass-through added for a module that doesn't need the full split (graduated-layering boilerplate); (2) the async .refine() in routes.ts checking that userId exists is a business invariant that belongs in the service, not in Zod validation; (3) the unread-count handler in routes.ts imports db/schema directly and queries the table itself instead of going through repository.ts.

assertions.name: flags-empty-passthrough-service
assertions.text: The review flags service.ts as an empty pass-through that adds no logic, unnecessary for a module this simple.

assertions.name: flags-business-invariant-in-refine
assertions.text: The review flags the async .refine() in routes.ts (checking the user exists) as a business invariant that belongs in the service layer, not in Zod shape validation.

assertions.name: flags-routes-importing-db-directly
assertions.text: The review flags the unread-count handler in routes.ts for importing db/schema directly and querying the table itself instead of going through repository.ts.
